sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: This visa allows you to play, coach, instruct or adjudicate for an Australian team, or do high level sports training with a sporting organisation. You and your family can stay in Australia for up to 2 years.

sections.heading: Overview > You must
sections.text:
- have a sponsor or supporter
- have a contract and a letter of support from a peak sporting body
- not work outside your specified sporting activities

Help with your visa

If you are getting help with your visa, before you pay someone, read information on Who can help with your visa application.

sections.heading: Overview > With this visa you can
sections.text:
- play, coach, adjudicate or instruct for an Australian team, or do high-level sports training with a sporting organisation
- stay for up to 2 years with members of the family unit
- apply for the visa in or outside Australia but not in immigration clearance

sections.heading: Overview > Cost
sections.text:
From

Exemptions may apply in limited circumstances, for more information, see About this visa.

sections.heading: Overview > Processing time
sections.text: For an indication of processing times for this visa, use the visa processing time guide tool. This will show the processing times for recently decided applications. It is a guide only and not specific to your application.

sections.heading: About this visa > With this visa, you can
sections.text:
- take part in a structured sports training program at the national or international level
- play for, coach, instruct or adjudicate for an Australian sporting team or sporting organisation for a season
- travel to and from Australia as many times as you want while your visa is valid
- include members of the family unit in your application

You can't do any work other than the approved sporting activity.

If you are coming to Australia as a member of an overseas sports team, you could apply for a Temporary Activity visa (subclass 408) Invited for Other Social and Cultural Activity.

sections.heading: About this visa > How long you can stay
sections.text:
This is a temporary visa. We grant the length of stay based on the activity we approve you to do on the visa.

If you are a sportsperson participating at local or regional competitions, then you will normally be expected to depart Australia at the end of the sporting season. The maximum stay for this visa stream is 2 years.

The visa is granted with multiple entry. You can leave and re-enter Australia as many times as you want while the visa is valid.

If you are overseas when the visa is granted, the visa stay period starts on the day that you enter Australia. If you are in Australia, the visa starts on the day that it is granted.

Your visa grant letter will tell you how long you can stay.

sections.heading: About this visa > Stay longer
sections.text: You can't stay in Australia longer by extending this visa. Explore your visa options.

sections.heading: About this visa > Include family
sections.text:
You can include members of the family unit in your application when you apply.

Family members who apply for the visa with you must also meet our health and character requirements.

sections.heading: About this visa > Cost
sections.text:
The visa costs for the main applicant.

There is also a charge for each family member who applies for the visa with you.

You might also have to pay other costs for health checks, police certificates and biometrics.

To work out what your visa will cost use the Visa Pricing Estimator. The estimator does not take into account the other costs.

Cost for eligible Pacific Island and Timor-Leste visa applicants

From 1 July 2026, a lower visa cost applies to eligible Pacific Island and Timor-Leste citizens who lodge a valid visa application.

We will charge eligible applicants the lower visa application cost during the application process in ImmiAccount. We will recognise eligible applicants by the valid passport from the specified countries used in the application when they apply.

Family members are also eligible for the lower visa cost. We base this on the passport of the primary applicant (or visa holder who satisfies the primary visa criteria).

The primary applicant must hold a valid passport issued by one of the following countries:

- Federated States of Micronesia
- Fiji
- Kiribati
- Nauru
- Palau
- Papua New Guinea
- Republic of the Marshall Islands
- Samoa
- Solomon Islands
- Timor-Leste
- Tonga
- Tuvalu

sections.heading: About this visa > Apply from
sections.text: You can be in or outside Australia, but not in immigration clearance, when you apply for the visa and when we decide on your application.

sections.heading: About this visa > Processing times
sections.text:
For an indication of processing times for this visa, use the visa processing time guide tool. This will show the processing times for recently decided applications. It is a guide only and not specific to your application.

Your application might take longer to process if:

- you don't fill it in correctly
- you don't include all the documents we need, or we need more information from you
- it takes us time to verify your information

We can't process your application if you don't pay the correct visa application charge. We will notify you if this is the case and if necessary return your application.

sections.heading: About this visa > Your obligations
sections.text:
You and your family must meet all visa conditions and follow Australian laws.

Learn more about conditions for this visa.

Your activities must not harm the work, training or job conditions of Australian citizens or permanent residents.

If your sponsor, supporting organisation or individual stops your activity or employment, you must do one of the following:

- if eligible, apply for a new visa
- leave Australia within 28 days of stopping work for your sponsor/supporter, or before your visa expires if that happens sooner

sections.heading: About this visa > Travel
sections.text:
You can travel outside Australia and return as many times as you want while the visa is valid.

The time you spend outside Australia does not extend the visa.

sections.heading: About this visa > Visa label
sections.text:
We will digitally link your visa to your passport. You will not get a label in your passport.

If we grant you a visa, we will send you a grant notification letter containing the visa grant number. You can use this number to access your digital visa record.

sections.heading: Eligibility
sections.text: You must meet all of the following eligibility criteria to be eligible for this visa.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have a supporter or sponsor > You need a supporter
sections.text:
You don't need a sponsor to apply for this visa if you:

- apply outside Australia, and
- intend to stay in Australia for less than 3 months

However, you must have a supporter who passes the support test to apply for this visa.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have a supporter or sponsor > You need a sponsor
sections.text:
You need a sponsor who is a temporary activities sponsor to apply for this visa if you:

- apply in Australia, or
- apply outside Australia and intend to stay in Australia for more than 3 months

sections.heading: Eligibility > Be an eligible sports trainee, elite player, coach, instructor or adjudicator > Apply as a sports trainee
sections.text:
You must:

- be able to show you currently compete or adjudicate at the Australian national level (or equivalent), or
- be endorsed by a relevant peak sporting body as having the potential to compete or adjudicate at the Australian national level (or equivalent)

sections.heading: Eligibility > Be an eligible sports trainee, elite player, coach, instructor or adjudicator > Apply as an elite player, coach, instructor or adjudicator
sections.text:
You must have an established reputation in your sporting field if you apply as:

- an elite player
- a coach
- an instructor
- an adjudicator

You must be endorsed by an Australian national sporting body as being able to play, coach, instruct or adjudicate the sport at a national level

sections.heading: Eligibility > Take part in full-time structured sports training, if applicable
sections.text: If you apply for this visa as a sports trainee, you must be undertaking full-time, structured sports training. The aim should be to achieve a high-performance outcome with an internationally recognised sports training organisation.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have a suitable formal agreement, if applicable
sections.text:
You must have a suitable formal agreement with your sporting club or sporting organisation in Australia if you apply for this visa as:

- an elite player
- a coach
- an instructor
- an adjudicator

sections.heading: Eligibility > Be able to support yourself and any dependants
sections.text: You must have enough money during your stay in Australia to support yourself and any dependent family members who travel to Australia with you.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Meet the health requirement
sections.text: You and any family members who apply for the visa with you must meet our health requirement.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Meet the character requirement
sections.text: You and family members aged 16 years and over who apply for the visa with you must meet our character requirement.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have adequate health insurance
sections.text:
You are personally liable for all your healthcare costs while you are in Australia. Medical insurance helps limit your financial liability.

You must have adequate health cover for the whole of your stay to be granted this visa. Your cover should cover you for medically necessary treatment, including transport.

See more about health insurance for overseas visitors.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have adequate health insurance > Reciprocal healthcare agreements
sections.text: Some countries have a reciprocal healthcare agreement with Australia. Find out more from Services Australia about reciprocal healthcare agreements.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Be a genuine temporary entrant
sections.text:
You can't use our temporary visa program to maintain ongoing residency in Australia.

The genuine temporary entrant (GTE) requirement helps us to make sure that you use temporary visas correctly.

We generally do not let temporary residents extend their stay in Australia beyond 4 years by applying for this visa.

We must be satisfied that you have a genuine intention to stay here temporarily.

When assessing your application, we will consider:

- your situation
- your immigration history
- previous compliance with visa conditions
- any other relevant matter

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have this visa
sections.text:
If you are in Australia, you can only apply for this visa if:

- you currently hold a substantive visa, or
- your last substantive visa ceased within the last 28 days.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have consent to be granted the visa
sections.text: We will only grant this visa to a child younger than 18 years if everyone who has parental responsibility for them has consented to us granting it.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Best interests of the child
sections.text: We might not grant this visa if it is not in the best interests of an applicant under 18.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have paid back debt to the Australian Government
sections.text: If you owe the Australian Government money, you must have paid it back or have a formal arrangement to pay it back.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Declare you have not paid for visa sponsorship
sections.text: When you apply for the visa, you must declare if you have ever engaged in conduct that could constitute a breach of the prohibition on paying for visa sponsorship.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Not had a visa cancelled or an application refused
sections.text:
We will consider your immigration history when we make a decision on your application. If you have had a visa cancelled or refused, you might not be eligible for this visa.

In some circumstances you may still apply for a permanent visa if you have had a visa cancelled or an application refused. See Limitations on applications in Australia.

If applying for a visa from outside Australia, see Can I go to Australia.

If you need help with immigration, see Who can help with your visa application.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Sign the Australian Values Statement
sections.text: If you are 18 years of age or older, you must acknowledge the Australian Values Statement. This confirms you will respect the Australian way of life and obey Australian laws when you apply for the visa. Learn more about Australian Values.

sections.heading: Step by step > Before you apply
sections.text:
You must have an eligible sponsor or supporter. Let us know if you are getting help with your application.

New step description

sections.heading: Step by step > Before you apply > Get help with your application
sections.text:
Only some people can help you with your application. If you appoint someone to give you immigration assistance they must be:

- a registered migration agent
- a legal practitioner, or
- an exempt person.

You can appoint anyone to receive documents on your behalf relating to your visa matter.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents
sections.text:
Provide evidence to support your application, including sponsor or supporter documents.

New step description

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Provide accurate information
sections.text: Provide accurate information. See what happens if you can't prove your identity or don't provide true information.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Identity documents
sections.text:
Provide the pages of your current passport showing your photo, personal details, and passport issue and expiry dates.

Also provide:

- a national identity card, if you have one
- proof of change of name

Documents that prove a change of name include:

- a marriage or divorce certificate
- change of name documents from an Australian Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, or the relevant overseas authority
- documents that show other names you have been known by

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Sponsor documents
sections.text:
If you are being sponsored for the visa, provide evidence your sponsor:

- is, or has applied to be, an approved temporary activities sponsor
- is an Australian organisation or government agency, or a foreign government agency lawfully operating in Australia, that administers or promotes sport or sporting events
- will meet their obligations to you and anyone who applies for the visa with you

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Supporter documents
sections.text:
You must provide evidence your supporter:

- is an Australian organisation or government agency or foreign government agency lawfully operating in Australia that administers or promotes sport or sporting events
- will meet their obligations to you and anyone who applies for the visa with you

Also provide your supporter's letter of endorsement

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Sports activity documents
sections.text: Provide evidence of your skills and abilities as a sportsperson, coach, instructor or adjudicator.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Sports activity documents > Sports trainee
sections.text:
Provide either:

- proof that you compete or adjudicate at the Australian national level, or
- a letter from a peak sporting body in Australia or overseas stating you have the ability to perform at the Australian national level

Also provide:

- proof that your training organisation has an international reputation for training elite sportspeople or adjudicators. You can't be sponsored or supported by a sports club that competes below the Australian national level
- details of the full-time training program you intend to undertake

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Sports activity documents > Elite player, coach, instructor or adjudicator
sections.text:
Provide your contract with the sponsoring organisation. It must state:

- the length of your contract
- what you will be paid
- your duties
- any organisations you will work with other than your supporter or sponsor
- your estimated hours of work
- any dependent family members also covered by the contract

Also provide a letter of endorsement from the Australian national sporting body that:

- supports the position
- confirms you have the ability to play, coach or instruct at the Australian national level

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Financial documents
sections.text:
Show us you can support yourself and anyone who comes to Australia on the visa with you by providing:

- an employment contract or bank statements, or
- evidence of your financial position from your bank or financial institution

We can also consider allowances, accommodation and other help from your employer.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Character documents
sections.text: We will tell you if and when you need to get a police certificate.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Tell us you are getting help
sections.text:
To nominate someone to:

- receive your correspondence, use Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient
- provide immigration assistance, use Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person.

Upload your written notification or your forms to ImmiAccount.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Partner documents
sections.text:
Provide your partner's:

- identity documents
- character documents
- marriage certificate
- documents about other relationships, if applicable

For de facto relationships provide either:

- evidence that your relationship is registered by an Australian State or Territory
- enough documents to prove you have been in a de facto relationship with your partner for at least 12 months before you apply

For both married and de facto applicants you must provide evidence that you are in a genuine and continuing relationship. Evidence can include but is not limited to:

- joint bank account statements
- billing accounts in joint names
- joint leases or mortgages
- documents that show your partner has lived at the same address as you

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Dependants under 18 documents
sections.text:
For every dependant 18 years old or younger who is applying with you, provide:

- copies of birth certificates or the family book showing the names of both parents of all your dependent children
- copies of the adoption paper, if applicable.

Parental responsibility documents

You must get consent for any applicant under 18 years of age to migrate to Australia from anyone who:

- has a legal right to decide where the child lives and
- is not coming to Australia with the child

They must complete either:

- Form 1229 Consent form to grant an Australian visa to a child under the age of 18 years
- a statutory declaration giving their consent for the child to visit Australia on this visa

Alternatively, you can show us:

- an Australian court order that allows your child to migrate to Australia, or
- that the laws of your home country allow them to migrate

Include:

- an identity document that shows the signature and photo of the person who completed the form or declaration, such as a passport or driver’s licence
- adoption papers or other court documents if applicable

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Dependants over 18 documents
sections.text:
To include your child who is over 18 in your visa application, they must be:

- over 18 years of age but not yet turned 23, and dependent on you or your partner, or
- over 23 years of age and unable to earn a living to support themselves due to physical or cognitive limitations and dependent on you or your partner

If your child is likely to turn 23 while your application is being processed, you will need to provide evidence they are dependent on you due to disability.

Provide:

- identity documents
- documents about their other relationships, if applicable
- character documents

You must also provide proof the child is dependent on you.

- proof of your relationship with the dependant such as a birth certificate or adoption papers
- a completed Form 47a Details of a child or other dependent family member aged 18 years or over
- proof of financial dependency such as bank statements, money transfers and rent receipts
- if the child is aged 23 or is likely to turn 23 while your application is being processed, you must also provide a report from a qualified medical practitioner that states they are dependent on you or your partner due to the total or partial loss of their bodily or mental functions

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > Translate
sections.text:
Have all non-English documents translated into English.

Provide original and translated documents in your application.

Translators in Australia must be accredited by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters.

Translators outside Australia do not have to be accredited. But on each translation, they must include their:

- full name
- address and telephone number
- qualifications and experience in the language they are translating

These details must be in English.

Note: You do not need to have any documents certified.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > Scan or photograph
sections.text:
Scan or photograph all documents (English and non-English) in colour.

The scans and photos must be clear.

If a document is more than one page, save it all as one file.

sections.heading: Step by step > Apply for the visa
sections.text:
You must apply for this visa online. You can be in or outside Australia when you apply.

New step description

sections.heading: Step by step > Apply for the visa > Apply online
sections.text:
Apply for the visa online in ImmiAccount.

- Create an account or log in to ImmiAccount
- Attach documents
- Have family applications processed together.
- Pay the application fee.
- Note the transaction reference number (TRN).

We will not process your application until you pay the charge.

Each family member must have their application charge paid and documents attached to their application.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply
sections.text:
We will let you know when we have received your application.

New step description

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Status updates
sections.text:
We can’t give updates on applications within the standard processing time.

You can check if we need more information from you in ImmiAccount.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Travel after you apply
sections.text:
If you are in Australia, you don't have to tell us if you want to travel outside Australia while we process your application. This is because you can be outside Australia when we make a decision. However, you cannot be in immigration clearance.

But if you leave Australia, make sure you have a valid visa to return.

Learn about visa expiry.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Health exams
sections.text: If you didn't have health examinations before you applied, we will let you know if you need them. Check ImmiAccount.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Biometrics
sections.text: We might ask for biometrics (fingerprints and photo). We will let you know if you need to provide them.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Attach more information
sections.text:
If you did not attach all documents when you applied, attach them as soon as possible in ImmiAccount.

We might also ask you to provide more information.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Stay lawful
sections.text:
If you are in Australia, make sure you stay lawful by holding a valid visa while we process your application.

If you were in Australia when you applied for this visa, you may be granted:

- a Bridging visa A (BVA) if you held a substantive visa when you applied
- a Bridging visa C (BVC) if you did not hold a substantive visa when you applied

If your current visa expires before we decide your application, the bridging visa will come into effect. You can stay in Australia on the bridging visa while we process your visa application. You can't re-enter Australia on a BVA or BVC - there is no right of return on these visas and they will cease on departure.

Learn more about visa expiry.

Check what conditions might apply to your bridging visa or the visa you have applied for with our condition checker.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Add family
sections.text:
You cannot add members of the family unit to your application after you have applied. If you do not include them in your application, your family members must apply separately.

To apply separately, your family members need to complete an application for a Temporary Activity, International Relations or Training Visa (Subsequent entrant) (403,407,408) form in ImmiAccount.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Add family > Subsequent entrants
sections.text:
If we grant you the visa, your family members can apply to join you in Australia as a subsequent entrant.

To apply as a subsequent entrant, your family members need to complete an application for a Temporary Activity, International Relations or Training Visa (Subsequent entrant) (403,407,408) form in ImmiAccount.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Add family > Newborn children
sections.text: Find out what to do if your child is born after you apply.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Mistakes on your application
sections.text:
Let us know as soon as you can if you made a mistake on your application.

Complete Form 1023 Notification of incorrect answers and attach it in ImmiAccount.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Help with your application
sections.text:
Let us know if you no longer want someone to:

- receive your correspondence - complete Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient
- provide immigration advice - complete Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person.

Upload your written notification or your forms to ImmiAccount.

For more information see Who can help you with your application.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Tell us if things change
sections.text:
Things you need to let us know about after you have applied include:

- changes to your phone number, email, address or passport
- changes to your marital or de facto status
- the birth of a child
- you want to withdraw your application

See how to tell us if your situation changes.

sections.heading: Step by step > Visa outcome
sections.text:
You can be in or outside Australia when we decide on your visa application.

We will let you know our decision in writing.

If we grant your visa, we will tell you:

- your visa grant number
- the date your visa starts
- your visa conditions, if applicable

Keep a copy of the decision.

If we refuse your visa, we will tell you:

- why we refused the visa
- whether you have a right to a review of the decision

We will not refund the application charge if we refuse your application.

New step description

sections.heading: When you have this visa > Coming to Australia
sections.text:
Before you travel

Check your travel documents

You must have:

- a valid visa to enter Australia
- a valid passport or other travel document.

At the border

Completing an Incoming Passenger Card

All people arriving in Australia must complete the Incoming Passenger Card. You will be given this card onboard.

Leaving the airport faster

We have an automated process that uses facial recognition technology and your ePassport. You might be able to leave the airport faster if you use SmartGate.

sections.heading: When you have this visa > In Australia
sections.text:
What you can do when you have this visa

- take part in a structured sports training program at the national or international level
- play for, coach, instruct or adjudicate for an Australian sporting team or sporting organisation for a season
- travel to and from Australia as many times as you want while your visa is valid.

You can't do any work other than the approved sporting activity.

To see your specific conditions and work entitlements use VEVO.

What you must do on this visa

You and your family members must meet all visa conditions and obey Australian laws.

See your conditions in VEVO.

Learn more about visa conditions and how they work.

Tell us if things change

Things you need to let us know about include:

- changes to your phone number, email, address or passport
- changes to your relationship status
- the birth of a child.

See how to tell us if there is a change in your situation.

See how long you can stay

The visa stay period starts on the date you enter Australia.

You can check your visa stay period in your visa grant letter or use VEVO.

To see when you must leave, use VEVO.

Staying longer

You can't stay in Australia longer by extending this visa. You must apply for a new visa if you want to stay longer.

See your options.

Travelling on your visa

You must make your first entry to Australia by the date specified in the visa grant letter. This is the Must not arrive after date.

Once you make your first entry to Australia your Visa stay period starts. Your Visa stay period is the length of time you can stay in Australia.

You can travel outside Australia and return as many times as you want during your Visa stay period while the visa is valid.

Time spent outside Australia does not extend the visa. The visa stay period does not start again each time you enter Australia. Any time you spend outside of Australia counts as part of the stay period.

See your conditions in VEVO.

Proving you have a visa

To prove you have a visa and show your conditions to someone, use VEVO.

Working

To see your conditions for work, use VEVO.

If you have permission to work, you are protected by Australian workplace law. See your workplace rights and entitlements.

Bringing family

Your family members who did not apply for the visa with you might be eligible to apply for a subsequent entrant visa.

Apply for a subsequent entrant visa using the Temporary Work and Activity Visa (Subsequent Entrant) (403,407,408) form in ImmiAccount.

sections.heading: When you have this visa > Leaving Australia
sections.text:
Before you leave

Check your travel documents

You must have a valid passport or other travel document to leave Australia.

Ensure your visa is still valid.

See what to do if your visa has expired or is about to expire.

At the border

Departures SmartGate

We have an automated process that uses facial recognition technology and your ePassport. You might be able to leave the airport faster if you use SmartGate.

After you leave

Getting your superannuation

You are likely to have some money in a superannuation fund if you worked in Australia and you are:

- aged 18 years or older
- paid AUD450 or more before tax in a month.

See how to access your super.

Proving you have been to Australia

To get proof of your travel in and out of Australia request your international movement records.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Overview > You must
sections.text:
- be an Australian organisation or government agency, or a foreign government agency lawfully operating in Australia, that administers or promotes sport or sporting events
- be able to meet your supporter or sponsor obligations

sections.heading: Sponsor > Overview > With this visa the applicant can
sections.text:
- play, coach, instruct or adjudicate for an Australian sporting team or organisation
- do high-level sports training

sections.heading: Sponsor > Overview > How long you can stay
sections.text: This is a temporary visa. The applicant can stay in Australia for up to 2 years.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Overview > Cost
sections.text:
to become a temporary activities sponsor.

There is no cost to sponsor someone for the visa after you are approved.

sections.heading: Sponsor > About this visa > Scope
sections.text:
You can support or sponsor an applicant and any family members who apply for the visa with them to travel to Australia:

- to play for, coach or adjudicate for an Australian team, or
- undertake high-level sports training organisation

Applicants who need a supporter

Applicants for this visa don't need a sponsor if they:

- apply outside Australia, and
- intend to stay in Australia for less than 3 months

However, these applicants need a supporter.

Applicants who need a sponsor

Applicants for this visa need a sponsor if they:

- apply in Australia, or
- apply outside Australia and intend to stay in Australia for more than 3 months

sections.heading: Sponsor > About this visa > Cost
sections.text:
It costs to apply to become an approved temporary activities sponsor.

There is no cost to sponsor someone for the visa after you are approved.

There is no cost to support a visa applicant.

sections.heading: Sponsor > About this visa > How long sponsorship lasts
sections.text: Your sponsorship normally last for 5 years.

sections.heading: Sponsor > About this visa > Sponsor obligations
sections.text:
You must meet your obligations as a temporary activities sponsor.

Your sponsorship obligations may last for a different period as specified by legislation. Learn more about your sponsorship obligations.

You are responsible for meeting these obligations even if you appoint someone, such as a migration agent, to act for you.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Eligibility
sections.text: You must meet all of the following eligibility criteria to be suitable to sponsor.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Eligibility > Support or sponsor an applicant
sections.text:
Applicants who need a supporter

Applicants for this visa don't need a sponsor if they:

- apply outside Australia, and
- intend to stay in Australia for less than 3 months

However, these applicants need a supporter. See more about supporter eligibility below.

Applicants who need a sponsor

Applicants for this visa need a sponsor if they:

- apply in Australia, or
- apply outside Australia and intend to stay in Australia for more than 3 months

See more about sponsor eligibility below.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Eligibility > Supporter eligibility > Meet the support test
sections.text:
To meet the support test:

- provide a letter of support on your organisation's letterhead
- we must not be aware of any adverse information about you or anyone associated with you that would affect your suitability as a supporter

The letter of support must identify:

- the visa applicant and any family members who intend to travel with them
- the work the applicant will take do
- what the applicant's activities will be
- when and where the applicant will be engaged

You don't need to submit an application to be a supporter.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Eligibility > Supporter eligibility > Be a certain kind of organisation
sections.text:
You must be an Australian organisation or government agency, or a foreign government agency lawfully operating in Australia, that administers or promotes sport or sporting events.

If you are supporting a sports trainee, your organisation:

- must have an international reputation for training elite sportspeople or adjudicators
- can't be a sporting club that primarily competes below the Australian national level for the sport

sections.heading: Sponsor > Eligibility > Sponsor eligibility > Meet the sponsorship test
sections.text:
You must be an approved temporary activities sponsor to sponsor an applicant for this visa.

You must meet the sponsorship test to sponsor a visa applicant. You must:

- be an approved sponsor
- agree in writing to sponsor the visa applicant and members of their family unit who intend to travel with them
- not withdraw that agreement

We must not know anything adverse about you, or a person or organisation associated with you, unless we can reasonably disregard it.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Eligibility > Sponsor eligibility > Be a certain kind of organisation
sections.text:
You must be an Australian organisation or government agency, or a foreign government agency lawfully operating in Australia, that administers or promotes sport or sporting events.

If you are sponsoring a sports trainee, your organisation:

- must have an international reputation for training elite sportspeople or adjudicators
- can't be a sporting club that primarily competes below the Australian national level for the sport

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > Before the applicant applies for the visa > Sponsors
sections.text:
If the applicant needs a sponsor you must be an approved temporary activities sponsor, or have submitted an application for approval as one.

You will also need to provide some documents to the applicant to submit with their visa application.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > Before the applicant applies for the visa > Supporters
sections.text:
Visa applicants who apply from outside Australia and intend to stay less than 3 months don't need a sponsor, but must have a supporter who meets the support test.

You will need to provide some documents to the applicant to submit with their visa application. You don't need to apply to become a supporter.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > Provide documents
sections.text:
Provide the visa applicant with evidence to support their visa application. They must submit these documents when they apply.

The documents you need to provide will depend on whether you are the applicant's sponsor or their supporter.

New step description

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > Provide documents > Sponsor documents > Evidence you are an approved sponsor
sections.text:
Provide the applicant with:

- your sponsorship approval letter, or
- evidence you have applied to be a temporary activities sponsor, such as your application ID or transaction reference number (TRN)

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > Provide documents > Sponsor documents > Evidence you are a certain kind of organisation
sections.text:
Provide evidence that you are an Australian organisation or government agency, or a foreign government agency lawfully operating in Australia, that administers or promotes sport or sporting events.

If you are sponsoring a sports trainee, provide evidence that your organisation has an international reputation for training elite sportspeople or adjudicators.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > Provide documents > Evidence you are a certain kind of organisation
sections.text: Provide evidence that you are a sporting organisation lawfully operating in Australia.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > Provide documents > Letter of invitation
sections.text:
Provide the applicant with a letter of invitation, on your organisation's letterhead if it has one, that includes:

- the name of the applicant and any dependants applying for the visa with them
- a description of the sporting activity or sports training they will be doing
- when that sporting activity or sports training will be done
- what the visa applicant will be doing as part of that sporting activity or sports training
- any payment or other support you will provide the applicant

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > After the applicant applies > Tell us if things change
sections.text: See how to let us know if your circumstances change.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > After the applicant applies > Withdraw sponsorship
sections.text: You must let us know in writing if you want to withdraw your sponsorship of a visa applicant.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > Visa outcome
sections.text:
We will let the visa applicant know our decision in writing.

New step description

sections.heading: Sponsor > When you have this visa > How long your sponsorship lasts
sections.text:
Approval as a temporary activities sponsor

Your approval as a temporary activities sponsor last for 5 years from the date we grant it unless we tell you otherwise.

You can apply to extend your sponsorship in ImmiAccount before it expires.

Sponsorship expiry reminders

From 1 July 2026, Temporary Activities Sponsors will receive an automated email reminder 90 days before their sponsorship expires. This will help avoid delays for sponsored visa applicants.

Ensure your sponsor contact details are up to date so you can receive these reminders.

sections.heading: Sponsor > When you have this visa > Your obligations
sections.text:
Temporary activity sponsor obligations

You must meet your obligations as a temporary activities sponsor. See more about temporary activities sponsor obligations.

You are responsible for meeting these obligations even if you appoint someone, such as a migration agent, to act for you.

Obligations as sponsor of a visa holder

You must also meet your obligations to the visa applicant you sponsor. These are to:

- absorb the cost of sponsorship, including migration agent costs, and not attempt to recover them from the visa holder
- ensure the visa holder does the activity in relation to which the visa was granted
- ensure the visa holder obeys licensing, registration and membership laws so they can continue to work in Australia

You might have to pay costs to find and remove the person you sponsor if they become unlawful.

sections.heading: Sponsor > When you have this visa > Withdraw sponsorship
sections.text: You can't withdraw your sponsorship or support of a visa holder after we grant the visa.

sections.heading: Sponsor > When you have this visa > Tell us if things change
sections.text:
You must email or post a letter to us using the contact details below if any of the following occurs:

- your address or contact details change
- the visa holder does not start in the position, program or activity for which the visa was granted
- the visa holder unexpectedly ends their position, program or activity for which the visa was granted
- any change to the formal arrangement or agreement with the visa holder
- you change the date that the visa holder will cease their position, program or activity
- you have paid the return travel cost of the visa holder
- the visa holder can't meet the requirements of their position, program or activity
- your legal entity ceases to exist
